name: Tadasana
description: Tadasana, or Mountain Pose, is the foundational posture for all standing yoga poses. It improves posture, strengthens thighs, knees, and ankles, and firms the abdomen and buttocks.
benefits: Improves posture and body awareness
Strengthens thighs, knees, and ankles
Firms abdomen and buttocks
Reduces flat feet symptoms
Develops core stability and balance
instructions: Stand with the bases of your big toes touching, heels slightly apart.
Engage your quadriceps and lift your kneecaps gently.
Lengthen your spine and draw your shoulder blades back and down.
Let your arms hang naturally by your sides with palms facing forward.
Gaze softly straight ahead and breathe evenly.
precautions: If you experience dizziness or have low blood pressure, stand with feet hip-width apart.

rules.feedback_message: Straighten your left leg gently without hyperextending
Straighten your right leg gently without hyperextending
Align your hips vertically over your ankles
Align your hips vertically over your ankles
Relax your left arm down along your torso
Relax your right arm down along your torso
Stand tall with your spine vertically aligned

name: Virabhadrasana II
description: Warrior II is a powerful standing posture that builds strength in the legs, opens the hips and chest, and develops endurance and concentration.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches legs and ankles
Stretches groins, chest, lungs, and shoulders
Stimulates abdominal organs
Increases stamina and physical stamina
Relieves backaches in second trimester of pregnancy
instructions: Stand with feet 3.5 to 4 feet apart.
Turn your left foot out 90 degrees and back right foot slightly in.
Bend your left knee directly over your left ankle until thigh is parallel to mat.
Extend both arms parallel to the floor, actively reaching outward.
Turn your head to look over the fingertips of your front left hand.
precautions: Those with neck issues should not turn head; gaze straight ahead. Keep front knee tracking over ankle.

rules.feedback_message: Bend your front left knee deeper toward 90 degrees
Keep your back right leg strong and fully straight
Raise your front left arm parallel to the floor
Extend your back right arm parallel to the floor
Straighten your left arm through the fingertips
Straighten your right arm through the fingertips
Keep your torso centered vertically between hips, do not lean forward

name: Vrikshasana
description: Vrikshasana replicates the graceful, rooted stance of a tree. It develops neurological balance, strengthens the legs, and calms the mind.
benefits: Strengthens thighs, calves, ankles, and spine
Stretches groins and inner thighs
Improves sense of balance and proprioception
Relieves sciatica and reduces flat feet
Enhances concentration and mental focus
instructions: Shift weight onto your right foot, grounding all four corners.
Bend your left knee and place the sole of left foot against your inner right calf or thigh (never on the knee).
Press foot and inner thigh into each other with equal pressure.
Bring palms together at chest center in Anjali Mudra or raise overhead.
Fix gaze on an unmoving point (Drishti) at eye level.
precautions: Avoid placing the foot directly on the knee joint. Use a wall for balance support if needed.

rules.feedback_message: Keep your standing right leg straight and firm
Open your bent left knee outward to the side
Bring palms together in prayer position at chest height
Bring palms together in prayer position at chest height
Keep your spine tall and maintain upright balance

name: Trikonasana
description: Triangle Pose provides a deep stretch to the hamstrings, groins, and hips while expanding the chest and lengthening the spine.
benefits: Stretches and strengthens thighs, knees, and ankles
Stretches hips, groins, hamstrings, and calves
Opens chest and shoulders
Stimulates abdominal organs
Helps relieve stress and improve digestion
instructions: Stand with feet 3.5 feet apart, turn right foot out 90 degrees.
Inhale, extend arms horizontally to the sides.
Exhale, reach right hand over right leg, bending from the hip joint.
Rest right hand on shin, ankle, or floor; extend left arm straight toward sky.
Keep both sides of the torso equally long.
precautions: Do not lock the front knee. If you have neck pain, look straight ahead instead of up at the top hand.

rules.feedback_message: Keep your lead right leg straight without locking the knee
Keep your back left leg grounded and straight
Reach your lower arm straight down toward your shin
Extend your top arm straight upward in line with shoulders
Straighten both arms fully
Straighten both arms fully

name: Utkatasana
description: Chair Pose strengthens the thighs, calves, and spine while opening the chest and shoulders. It is a dynamic, energizing posture.
benefits: Strengthens ankles, calves, thighs, and spine
Stretches shoulders and chest
Stimulates abdominal organs, diaphragm, and heart
Builds mental discipline and lower body stamina
instructions: Stand in Tadasana with feet together or hip-width apart.
Inhale and raise arms perpendicular to the floor past your ears.
Exhale and bend knees as if sitting back into an imaginary chair.
Keep thighs as parallel to the floor as possible.
Draw lower back long and keep chest lifted.
precautions: Avoid if suffering from recent knee or low back injuries. Keep knees behind toe tips.

rules.feedback_message: Sink hips lower and bend knees toward 90 degrees
Sink hips lower and bend knees toward 90 degrees
Hinge hips backward as if sitting in a low chair
Hinge hips backward as if sitting in a low chair
Reach arms straight up alongside your ears

name: Bhujangasana
description: Cobra Pose is a gentle backbend that opens the chest, strengthens the spine, and invigorates the nervous system.
benefits: Strengthens the spine and back muscles
Stretches chest, lungs, shoulders, and abdomen
Firms the buttocks and stimulates digestive organs
Helps relieve stress and fatigue
Improves spinal flexibility
instructions: Lie prone on the mat with tops of feet flat on floor.
Place palms on the mat under your shoulders, elbows hugged close to ribs.
Inhale, press tops of feet into mat, and gently lift chest off the ground.
Keep shoulders relaxed away from ears and broad across collarbones.
Hold and breathe smoothly.
precautions: Avoid during pregnancy or if suffering from carpal tunnel syndrome or severe back issues.

rules.feedback_message: Lift your chest off the mat using your upper back muscles
Lift your chest off the mat using your upper back muscles
Keep elbows slightly bent and tucked close to ribs

name: Balasana
description: Child's Pose is a restful resting posture that gently stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles while calming the central nervous system.
benefits: Gently stretches hips, thighs, and ankles
Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and fatigue
Relieves back and neck pain when supported
Normalizes breathing rate and lowers heart rate
instructions: Kneel on the floor with big toes touching, knees wide apart.
Sit hips back onto heels, exhale, and lay torso down between thighs.
Extend arms straight forward on the mat or alongside torso.
Rest your forehead gently on the mat.
Breathe deeply into the back of your lungs.
precautions: If suffering from knee injuries or diarrhea, place a folded blanket between calves and thighs.

rules.feedback_message: Fold hips completely back onto your heels
Fold hips completely back onto your heels
Rest your belly comfortably between thighs
Extend arms forward comfortably on the mat

name: Adho Mukha Svanasana
description: One of the most widely recognized yoga poses, Downward-Facing Dog rejuvenates the entire body, strengthening the upper body while stretching the hamstrings and calves.
benefits: Strengthens arms, shoulders, and legs
Stretches shoulders, hamstrings, calves, and arches
Energizes the body and stimulates blood flow
Calms the brain and helps relieve mild depression
instructions: Start on all fours with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Tuck toes, exhale, and lift knees away from floor.
Push sit bones toward sky, lengthening spine into an inverted V shape.
Press firmly through palms and draw heels toward the mat.
Keep head between upper arms without letting it dangle excessively.
precautions: Avoid with high blood pressure or late-term pregnancy. Bend knees if hamstrings are tight.

rules.feedback_message: Lift sit bones high to form an inverted V shape
Lift sit bones high to form an inverted V shape
Straighten legs gently without forcing heels down

name: Setu Bandhasana
description: Bridge Pose opens the chest, heart, and shoulders while strengthening the spine, glutes, and hamstrings.
benefits: Stretches the chest, neck, and spine
Calms the brain and helps alleviate stress
Stimulates abdominal organs, lungs, and thyroid
Rejuvenates tired legs and improves digestion
instructions: Lie supine on the floor, bend knees, and set feet flat on floor hip-distance apart.
Exhale and press feet and arms firmly into floor.
Lift hips toward sky until thighs are about parallel to floor.
Clasp hands under pelvis and extend through arms.
Keep thighs and inner feet parallel.
precautions: Avoid turning head while in the pose to protect the cervical spine. Avoid with neck injuries.

rules.feedback_message: Keep knees stacked directly above ankles

Press through feet to lift hips high toward the ceiling

name: Dhanurasana
description: Bow Pose is an energizing backbend where the body arches like an archer's bow, stretching the entire front body and toning the back.
benefits: Stretches the entire front of the body, ankles, thighs, and groins
Strengthens back muscles and improves posture
Stimulates abdominal organs and neck glands
Relieves mild backache and fatigue
instructions: Lie on your belly with hands alongside torso, palms up.
Exhale, bend knees, and bring heels as close as possible to buttocks.
Reach back with hands and clasp your ankles.
Inhale, strongly lift heels up and away from buttocks while lifting chest.
Keep gaze forward and breathe evenly into your belly.
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high or low blood pressure, hernia, or recent abdominal surgery.

rules.feedback_message: Bend knees and kick feet upward into hands
Bend knees and kick feet upward into hands
Reach back, hold ankles, and lift chest up

name: Natarajasana
description: Dedicated to Lord Shiva as the cosmic dancer, this pose combines balance, backbending, and hip opening with poise and grace.
benefits: Stretches shoulders, chest, thighs, groins, and abdomen
Strengthens legs and ankles
Develops graceful balance, core stability, and focus
Increases spinal mobility
instructions: Stand in Tadasana, shift weight onto right foot.
Bend left knee, reaching left hand back to grasp inner left ankle.
Inhale, extend right arm straight up toward ceiling.
Exhale, kick left foot up and back, hinging slightly forward from hip.
Keep chest open and fix gaze on a steady point ahead.
precautions: Keep standing knee unlocked. Avoid if you have acute low back pain or balance disorders.

rules.feedback_message: Keep standing right leg strong and steady
Kick lifted left foot back and high into your hand
Extend forward arm forward at eye level
Hinge slightly forward while opening chest

name: Sukhasana
description: Sukhasana is a comfortable seated posture for meditation and pranayama that promotes grounded posture and mental calm.
benefits: Calms the brain and relieves mental tiredness
Strengthens the back and lengthens the spine
Stretches the knees and ankles
Encourages steady diaphragmatic breathing
instructions: Sit on the floor or cushion, crossing shins with feet under opposite knees.
Rest hands on knees with palms up (Gyan Mudra) or palms down.
Elongate spine upward from tailbone through crown of head.
Draw shoulders back and down, softening facial muscles.
Close eyes and focus on the natural rhythm of your breath.
precautions: Sit on a folded blanket or yoga block if hips are tight or knees are higher than hips.

Sit tall with your spine elongated and shoulders relaxed
Rest hands gently on knees
